My Story

Lyric
Hermanson

Coach. Creator. Work in progress.
"The behaviors I learned in the gym changed every other area of my life."

I am not a coach who read a book and decided to help people. I am a coach who lived through the hardest version of what my clients are going through. And made it out on the other side.

Everything I teach, I have tested on my own life. And my life has been the lab.

I have been homeless. I have struggled with addiction: alcohol, substances, pornography. I have battled a binge eating disorder while trying to compete as a bodybuilder. I grew up in circumstances that gave me every reason to expect less from myself.

And at the same time, I have been a 4.0 student. A competitive athlete. A role model. A content creator with over 600,000 people watching me show up every single day. I have changed lives, coached athletes, and built something from nothing.

That is not a contradiction. That is what it looks like to be high-functioning and still falling apart on the inside. And it is exactly who I coach.

The gym didn't save me. The behaviors did.

I used to think the gym was about the body. Calories, reps, progress photos. But what the gym actually gave me was a daily practice of showing up when I didn't want to. Of doing hard things on purpose. Of building identity through action instead of waiting to feel ready.

Those behaviors (discipline, consistency, accountability, purpose) transferred into every area of my life. Sobriety. Relationships. Faith. School. Business. The gym was just where I learned them first.

That is what I teach. Not fitness. Not a program. The behavioral foundation that makes everything else possible.

Where I am now.

I am fully sober. I am competing as a natural bodybuilder. I am a contracted athlete, a content creator, a coach, and a man of faith. I am 21 years old and I have already rebuilt my life more times than most people do in a lifetime.

I am not perfect. I am not finished. But I am someone who knows what it takes to become someone different, and I am someone who can walk alongside you while you do it.
